prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1011; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe that occurred while changing lanes on a multi-lane road, with the other vehicle moving into the claimant's lane and making contact along the passenger side. The claimant is unrepresented and provided an initial statement by phone, describing neck and back pain beginning shortly after the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant and the damage pattern on the vehicle, which lines up with the described impact along the side panels and mirror. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The driver is shown as a named driver on the policy.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the lane change and the contact between the two vehicles. Two independent witnesses in nearby vehicles gave statements that match the claimant's account of how the collision happened.

Entry 4: Medical records show the claimant was seen for neck and back strain, with the type and level of injury fitting the force of a side impact. No prior injury to the same body areas is on record. Treatment followed a typical course and eased off as the claimant improved.

Entry 5: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far. It is not yet fully clear from the statements and photos exactly where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at the moment of impact, so I have requested a follow-up question on seating position.

Entry 6: Based on the photos, witness statements, the other driver's confirmation, and the medical picture, the claim is consistent across sources and I am recommending it proceed to standard settlement review, with the seating position question noted as the only open item.
